previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting, found to be due to diabetic ketoacidosis. She was transferred from the ED to the MICU for management, where she received IV fluids, insulin drip, and electrolyte repletion. The insulin drip was discontinued and transitioned to subcutaneous U100 Regular insulin due to community pharmacy availability. Her blood glucose stabilized, and she tolerated oral intake. Chronic abdominal pain was managed with her home Dilaudid regimen. Social work secured temporary housing. She received diabetes education and was discharged home with a 7-day medication supply, follow-up appointments, and instructions for ongoing care.
problems: Diabetes with ketoacidosis, type I [juvenile type], uncontrolled

# DM1: Pt had mild DKA on presentation. Managed with IV insulin 
x 1 in the ED, but gap improved rapidly. ___ have been triggered 
by infection, but likely exacerbated by not taking insulin in 
the setting of subjective weakness and poor po intake. Spoke 
with ___ and Pharmacy about Pt's U500. Apparently, she has 
been getting 35 units worth (ie 35 regular human insulin 
equivalents) of U500, not 35 units OF U500 (ie 175 regular human 
insulin equivalents). She has actually been hypoglycemic on 35 
regular human insulin equivalents tid. ___ adjusted insulin 
to be less aggressive during lunch and dinner (35 B, 25 L, 20 D, 
regular insulin units). Pt was stable but somewhat hyperglycemic 
on this regimen w/ blood sugars in high 200s to 300s, but Pt had 
been refusing sliding scale correction. Pt started to eat a 
normal diet on ___ evening and had a full breakfast and 
lunch w/out exacerbating her abdominal pain. She was discharged 
on her current regimen and instructed about the importance of 
using the current lower dosing of her insulin instead of her 
regular insulin until her outpatient providers could adjust it 
as she is taking more orally. She expressed understanding and 
said that she would keep her PCP and ___ appointments. Pt's 
electrolytes were stable after the first two days of admission, 
and she did not require further repletion.

# Abd Pain, n/v/d: Could be ___ infectious gastoenteritis vs 
DKA. However, pt endorses Sx x 1 week, and viral gastroenteritis 
not expected to last that long. Pt endorses ""burning"" with po 
intake and epigastric tenderness on ED exam, so gastritis is 
possible.  She was placed on bid pantoprazole 40mg IV, but still 
experienced her discomfort ""at the bottom of her stomach."" She 
also reported a consistent RUQ dull pain, but her LFTs were 
normal aside from mild elevation of her AP. She is s/p 
cholecystectomy, and had a RUQ ultrasound that did not show any 
abnormalities. Her home po hydromorphone (6mg po q3 hrs PRN) was 
continued, and she received NO IV narcotics based on limits that 
have previously been set w/ her PCP and other care providers. 
She also received metoclopromide and ondansetron for nauesa. Her 
pain improved and she tolerated a normal diet the evening before 
and day of discharge.

# dizziness: Pt reported intermittent dizziness of unclear 
etiology. Question of otolith and BPPV or more likely 
pharmacological effect from some of her anti-emetics. Pt was not 
orthostatic, and symptoms seemed to resolve on day of discharge.

# psych: Has been difficult to care for given borderline 
personality disorder. Pt's home medications including diazepam 
and mirtazipine were continued. 
 
# asthma: Con't home meds

TRANSITIONAL ISSUES:
-Pt's insulin regimen on discharge was significantly lower than 
her prior home dose (less than half). This is most likely due to 
reduced PO intake and will need to be adjusted.
-consider further workup of intermittent dizziness if persistent
